packages.recipeChange: in-place rewrite of the published 2.1.25156 recipe at the maintainer's direction (single-user source, no -piko.N revision): rfde6aa0d5229a522 (commit 389bf8d) dropped the winfsp-setup entry and declared the admin recipe; r6654752550700411 (commit 722bcf4) corrected the post-install verification to the side-by-side FSD instance key

adminRecipe.remove: piko-admin.ps1 remove: elevated msiexec /x <saved MSI> /qn /norestart, then asserts registry entry, WinFsp.Launcher and all WinFsp+* instance keys are gone
adminRecipe.ownership: expected version is read from the MSI ProductVersion property via Windows Installer COM (no hardcoded version); a registered WinFsp at another version is refused for both install and removal
adminRecipe.postInstallChecks: registry uninstall entry DisplayVersion == MSI ProductVersion; Get-Service WinFsp.Launcher; at least one HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\WinFsp+* FSD instance key

notes: The interactive winfsp-setup entry is gone: every driver install now goes through an explicitly approved Administrator-terminal run and leaves a Piko receipt, so uninstall always knows what it owns. The first live run proved the value of the receipt model: a wrong script assertion failed loudly with a recorded receipt and a blocked uninstall instead of silently claiming success.
